item.title: Lateral Reading vs. Vertical Review: Fact-Checking AI Claims Beyond the Chat
item.description:
Lateral Reading vs. Vertical Review: Fact-Checking AI Claims Beyond the Chat

Relying on an artificial intelligence model to generate content is becoming standard practice in research, journalism, and business operations. However, the default mode of consumption—reading a response from top to bottom—is fundamentally flawed when assessing truthfulness. This method, known as vertical review, creates an illusion of understanding that often masks hallucinations and fabricated data.

Fact-Checking AI Content Before Publishing: The Source Ladder Method

The integration of Large Language Models (LLMs) into editorial workflows has accelerated content production, but it has also introduced a critical vulnerability: hallucination. When you ask “how to fact check ai content before publishing,” the answer is not merely running spellcheck or trusting citations. AI models synthesize information from training data, which can include outdated facts, fabricated sources, or biased interpretations.
